input.quote: Such inspections may be made no more than once each calendar year, at reasonable times and upon reasonable notice. Commerce One shall bear all costs and expenses of such inspection. If any such inspection discloses a shortfall or an overpayment, the appropriate party shall promptly pay the amount of such shortfall or refund such overpayment. In addition, if any such inspection reveals an underpayment of more than five percent (5%) for the period under audit, Corio shall reimburse Commerce One for the reasonable cost of the examination.
input.rationale: Section 4.4 is the only audit right binding us (Corio). It meets or exceeds the preferred position on every material term: frequency is capped at once each calendar year; the audit is limited to an off-site review of books and records maintained for fee-verification purposes, with no right of access to Corio systems or premises-level inspection; it must be conducted by an independent certified public accountant who is reasonably acceptable to us (a stronger control than the preferred "independent auditor"); it must occur at reasonable times; Commerce One bears all costs unless an underpayment exceeding 5% is found; and the true-up runs both ways, so a discovered overpayment must be refunded to us. The only sub-element short of the preferred wording is that notice is "reasonable notice" rather than a fixed 30 (or fallback 15) days, and auditor confidentiality is handled generally through Section 10 and the concurrent non-disclosure agreement rather than expressly in the audit clause. Those are minor drafting points, not material failures of the fallback, so no redline is warranted; we would only raise the fixed notice period if the clause is reopened for other reasons.
